target_customer: Large tech platforms, marketplaces and payments companies that run trust and safety, risk and compliance review
problem: Platforms rely on large outsourced human review teams for fraud, harassment and policy enforcement, which is costly, traumatic work that cannot keep up with volume.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API for AI review agents and decision models, with expert labeled data offered more recently
product_category: AI agents for trust and safety, risk and compliance

founders.name: David Graunke
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built the policy and workflow engine scaling Stripe from internal reviewers to thousands of outsourced vendor agents.

founders.name: Steven Guichard
previous_startups: Thomas Street (software design and engineering consultancy)

competitors.name: Spectrum Labs
competitors.what: AI content moderation, launched a product for generative AI content in April 2023

technical_complexity.rationale: Building policy engines and prompting or fine tuning language models for review accuracy at large platform scale, using the founders' Stripe experience, is demanding applied engineering but not research grade.

defensibility.rationale: Embedded workflows and policy specific labeled decisions create some lock in and data advantage, while the underlying models are available to anyone.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ActiveFence acquired Spectrum Labs in September 2023, consolidating rivals; no incumbent is reported to have displaced SafetyKit.

market_need_then: Large platforms relied on outsourced reviewers and the founders saw the pain at Stripe and Airbnb. Layoffs in in-house trust and safety teams in 2023 pushed work toward vendors, per press coverage found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B, earlier humane framing about ending traumatic manual toil, later 'the ground truth for Trust and Safety teams'.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and clear to buyers but generic, with no brand specific press found. Credibility comes from named customers and investors instead.

outcome_analysis: SafetyKit raised a 27 million dollar Series A in 2025 per the YC page and trackers, backed by Ribbit, First Round and YC, and lists marquee customers such as Patreon, Eventbrite, Upwork and Substack. Founders came from Stripe risk review, matching the buyer's pain. No acquisition or shutdown was found. Its site now emphasizes expert labeled data, suggesting positioning has widened since the batch.
notes: Series A date conflicts: trackers say April 4, 2025 while the YC page news item is dated June 2, 2025, so only the year is recorded; lead investor also varies by source. Earlier seed (about 4M, late 2023, First Round and Liquid 2) and pre-seed (500K, Sept 2023) appear only on aggregators, so unverified and not recorded. A third founder, Alex Rosenblatt, appears in one aggregator but not on the YC page, so is not listed. Customer lists differ between YC page and company site. Education not found.
